'''Ichinomiya Gozen Shrine''' (一之御前神社) is a shrine located in {{ill|Aichi Prefecture|en|Aichi Prefecture|qid=Q80434|lt=Aichi Prefecture}}, {{ill|Nagoya|ady|Нагоя|af|Nagoja|am|ናጎያ|an|Nagoya|ar|ناغويا|arz|ناجويا|ast|Nagoya|az|Naqoya|azb|ناقویا، آیچی|ba|Нагоя|ban|Nagoya|be|Нагоя|be_x_old|Нагоя|bew|Nagoya|bg|Нагоя|bn|নাগোইয়া|br|Nagoya|bs|Nagoya|ca|Nagoya|ce|Нагоя|ceb|Nagoya-shi|ch|Nagoya|chr|ᎾᎪᏯ|chy|Nagoya|ckb|ناگۆیا|cs|Nagoja|cy|Nagoya|da|Nagoya|de|Nagoya|ee|Nagoya|el|Ναγκόγια|eo|Nagojo|es|Nagoya|et|Nagoya|eu|Nagoya|fa|ناگویا|fi|Nagoya|fj|Nagoya|fo|Nagoya|fr|Nagoya|frr|Nagoya|ga|Nagoya|gl|Nagoia|got|𐌽𐌰𐌲𐌰𐌿𐌹𐌰|ha|Nagoya|hak|Nagoya-sṳ|he|נגויה|hi|नागोया|hr|Nagoja|hu|Nagoja|hy|Նագոյա|iba|Nagoya|id|Nagoya|ik|Nagoya|ilo|Nagoya|io|Nagoya|is|Nagoya|it|Nagoya|ja|名古屋市|jv|Nagoya|ka|ნაგოია|kaa|Nagoya|ki|Nagoya|kk|Нагоя|ko|나고야시|ky|Нагоя|la|Nagoya|lad|Nagoya|lg|Nagoya|lt|Nagoja|lv|Nagoja|mdf|Нагоя|mg|Nagoya|mi|Nagoya|mk|Нагоја|ml|നഗോയ|mn|Нагоя|mr|नागोया|ms|Nagoya|my|နာဂိုယာမြို့|mzn|ناگویا، آیچی|nl|Nagoya|nn|Nagoya|no|Nagoya|ny|Nagoya|or|ନାଗୋୟା|os|Нагоя|pa|ਨਾਗੋਯਾ|pam|Nagoya, Aichi|pl|Nagoja|pms|Nagoya|pnb|ناگویا|pnt|Ναγκόγια|pt|Nagoia|qu|Nagoya|ro|Nagoya|ru|Нагоя|sah|Нагоя|sat|ᱱᱟᱹᱜᱚᱭᱟ|sc|Nagoya|sco|Nagoya|sd|ناگويا|sh|Nagoya|si|නගෝයා|simple|Nagoya|sk|Nagoja|sl|Nagoja|sr|Нагоја|ss|INagoya|su|Nagoya, Aichi|sv|Nagoya|sw|Nagoya|szl|Nagoja|ta|நகோயா|tg|Нагоя|th|นาโงยะ|tl|Nagoya|tn|Nagoya|tok|ma tomo Nakoja|tr|Nagoya|tt|Нагоя|tum|Nagoya|tw|Nagoya|ug|ناگويا|uk|Наґоя|ur|ناگویا|uz|Nagoya|vep|Nagoi|vi|Nagoya|vo|Nagoya|war|Nagoya|wo|Nagoya|wuu|名古屋市|zea|Nagoya|zh|名古屋市|zh_classical|名古屋市|zh_min_nan|Nagoya-chhī|zh_yue|名古屋|qid=Q11751|lt=Nagoya}}, {{ill|Atsuta-ku, Nagoya|ar|أتسوتا-كو|ca|Atsuta-ku|ceb|Atsuta-ku|es|Atsuta-ku (Nagoya)|fa|آتسوتا-کو، ناگویا|fr|Atsuta-ku|id|Atsuta-ku, Nagoya|it|Atsuta-ku|ja|熱田区|ko|아쓰타구|pl|Atsuta (Nagoja)|th|เขตอัตสึตะ|tl|Atsuta-ku, Nagoya|tr|Atsuta|uk|Район Ацута|ur|اتسوتا وارڈ، ناگویا|vi|Atsuta, Nagoya|zh|热田区|qid=Q1355625|lt=Atsuta Ward}}. It is one of the {{ill|Keidai-Sessha|ja|Keidai-Sessha}} of {{ill|Atsuta Shrine|en|Atsuta Shrine|qid=Q482065|lt=Atsuta Shrine}}.

==Overview==
The founding is said to have occurred either during the era of {{ill|Emperor Keikō|en|Emperor Keikō|qid=Q329723|lt=Keikō Emperor}} or during the reign of {{ill|Emperor Tenmu|ja|Emperor Tenmu|2=ja|3=天武天皇|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenmu Emperor|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Tenmu|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q335181}} {{#tag:ref|"‘The palace of the Sun (Emperor Keikō) and the establishment of a separately enshrined Aramitama deity’ (from "Atsuta Shrine Historical Records: Compilation of Origins": page 139)"|group="Note"}}. It is located to the northwest of the main shrine, at the far end of the pilgrimage path known as "Kokoro no Komichi", and was relocated to its present site in {{ill|1893|ab|1893|af|1893|als|1893|am|1893 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|1893|ar|1893|ary|1893|arz|1893|ast|1893|av|1893|avk|1893|az|1893|azb|۱۸۹۳ (میلادی)|ba|1893 йыл|ban|1893|bar|1893|bat_smg|1893|bcl|1893|be|1893|be_x_old|1893|bg|1893|bn|১৮৯৩|bpy|মারি ১৮৯৩|br|1893|bs|1893.|ca|1893|cdo|1893 nièng|ce|1893 шо|ceb|1893|ckb|١٨٩٣|crh|1893|cs|1893|csb|1893|cv|1893|cy|1893|da|1893|de|1893|diq|1893|el|1893|eml|1893|eo|1893|es|1893|et|1893|eu|1893|fa|۱۸۹۳|fi|1893|fiu_vro|1893|fo|1893|fr|1893|frp|1893|frr|1893|fur|1893|fy|1893|ga|1893|gan|1893年|gcr|1893|gd|1893|gl|1893|gn|1893|gv|1893|he|1893|hi|१८९३|hif|1893|hr|1893.|hsb|1893|ht|1893 (almanak gregoryen)|hu|1893|hy|1893|hyw|1893 թուական|ia|1893|id|1893|ilo|1893|inh|1893 шу|io|1893|is|1893|it|1893|ja|1893年|jv|1893|ka|1893|kaa|1893|kk|1893 жыл|kn|೧೮೯೩|ko|1893년|krc|1893 джыл|ksh|Joohr 1893|ku|1893|kv|1893-ӧд во|la|1893|lb|1893|lez|1893 йис|li|1893|lij|1893|lmo|1893|lt|1893 m.|lv|1893. gads|mai|१८९३|map_bms|1893|mdf|1893|mg|1893|mhr|1893|mi|1893|min|1893|mk|1893|ml|1893|mr|इ.स. १८९३|mrj|1893 и|ms|1893|my|၁၈၉၃|myv|1893 ие|mzn|۱۸۹۳|nah|1893|nap|1893|nds|1893|new|ई सं १८९३|nl|1893|nn|1893|no|1893|nov|1893|nrm|1893|nso|1893|oc|1893|olo|1893|or|୧୮୯୩|os|1893-æм аз|pa|1893|pap|1893|pl|1893|pnb|1893|pt|1893|qu|1893|ro|1893|ru|1893 год|rue|1893|sa|१८९३|sah|1893 сыл|sc|1893|scn|1893|sco|1893|sd|1893ع|se|1893|sh|1893.|shn|1893|simple|1893|sk|1893|sl|1893|smn|1893|sq|1893|sr|1893|stq|1893|su|1893|sv|1893|sw|1893|szl|1893|ta|1893|te|1893|tg|Соли 1893|th|พ.ศ. 2436|tk|1893|tl|1893|tly|1893|tr|1893|tt|1893 ел|udm|1893 ар|ug|1893 - يىلى|uk|1893|ur|1893ء|uz|1893|vec|1893|vi|1893|vls|1893|vo|1893|wa|1893|war|1893|wuu|1893年|xmf|1893|yi|1893|za|1893 nienz|zea|1893|zh|1893年|zh_classical|一八九三年|zh_min_nan|1893 nî|zh_yue|1893年|qid=Q7840|lt=1893}} (Meiji 26); prior to that, it stood near the southeast of the current main shrine {{#tag:ref|"From the perspective of the former main hall, the direction was still to the northwest. (From "April 1893 Atsuta Shrine Reconstruction and Pre-Meiji Structures Location Estimation Diagram": <ref name="名古屋市史地図">"Nagoya City History Map"</ref>)"|group="Note"}}.

It enshrines '''Amaterasu Omikami Aramitama''' (あまてらすおおかみあらみたま) as its deity<ref name="神宮20"/>. The term “Aramitama” refers to a divine spirit that generates fierce, dynamic phenomena and is seen as a symbol of valor and initiative. The reason for its enshrinement at Atsuta Shrine is understood to be equivalent to the existence of {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|en|Ise Shrine|qid=Q687168|lt=Ise Grand Shrine}}’s {{ill|Aramatsuri-no-Miya|es|Aramatsuri no miya|fr|Aramatsuri no miya|ja|荒祭宮|qid=Q2859485}} <small>({{Coord|34|27|22|N|136|43|30|E|scale:2500}})</small><ref name="神宮20"/>.

Referred to as "‘The First Attendant Deity of the Imperial Court’" {{#tag:ref|"From 'Atsuta Shrine Official Enshrinement Record' <ref name="神宮史料縁起由緒139"/> and 'Atsuta Shrine Record' <ref name="神宮史料縁起由緒363">"Atsuta Shrine Historical Records: Compilation of Origins": page 363</ref>, etc."|group="Note"}}, the shrine not only shares an extremely close relationship with the main shrine but also gives the impression of a loyal, trusted aide. During the main shrine’s rituals, it was long customary to first present offerings here—a practice said to carry the meaning of "oni-gui" (poison tasting) {{#tag:ref|"‘When enshrining the main shrine, offerings are first prepared at Aramisaki, as is commonly said to be 'oni-gui’" (from "Oshu Shrine Secret Tradition": <ref name="神宮史料縁起由緒続一7">"Atsuta Shrine Historical Records: Continued Compilation of Origins (Part I)": page 7</ref>)"|group="Note"}}.
<br/>From this, an alternative theory has long existed proposing that, either as a different deity or as a supplementary spirit, {{ill|Ootomo Takehito no Mikoto|ja|大伴武日命}} was enshrined. While {{ill|Amano Sadakage|ja|天野信景|qid=Q6535030}} and {{ill|Fukada Masakazu|ja|深田正韶}} support this theory, {{ill|Tsuda Masanari|ja|津田正生|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsuda Masao|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q22123474}} dismisses it as "inconceivable"<ref name="地名考75">"Owari Province Place Name Studies": page 75</ref>. According to the "Owari Chronicle", Ootomo Takehito no Mikoto was a warrior who, during Yamato Takeru’s eastern expedition, served as a deputy general on both flanks alongside {{ill|Kibi no Takehiko|ja|吉備武彦命|lt=Kibi Takehiko no Mikoto}} (きびたけひこのみこと) {{#tag:ref|"From the Nihon Shoki (Volume 7, Emperor Keikō)"<ref name="日本書紀上289">"Kazana Nihon Shoki, Volume 1": page 289</ref>|group="Note"}}, and it is said that the placement of this shrine and {{ill|Ryujinja|ja|龍神社 (熱田神宮)|lt=Ryujinja|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ryujinja|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|qid=Q135579187}} (whose enshrined deity is Kibi Takehiko no Mikoto) flanking the main shrine like guards originates from this account<ref name="尾張志熱田9">"Owari Chronicle Atsuta": page 9</ref>.
<br/>Before the Edo period, it appears that Ryujinja and this shrine were regarded as a combined entity, and a petition requesting that they be recognized as separate shrines was submitted to the chief priest (dated June 5, 1686 ({{ill|1686|ja|貞享3|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jōkyō 3|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|qid=Q135579188}} April 15))<ref name="神宮史料造営遷宮上412">"Atsuta Shrine Historical Records: Construction and Relocation, Volume I": page 412</ref>{{#tag:ref|"Request stating 'Separate shrines for Ichinomiya and Ryujinja'."|group="Note"}}. This request was granted, and since then, Ichinomiya Gozen Shrine and Ryujinja have existed independently.

As for the origin of the shrine’s name, works such as {{ill|Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|ja|倭姫命世記|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wahimeimyojoseki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q131331326}} note that the character "魂" can be read as "Misaki", giving rise to the theory that it was written as "Ichinomisaki" (一ノ魂) {{#tag:ref|"From 'Atsuta Main and Subsidiary Shrine Divine Body Sacred Decree Collection Theory'"<ref name="神宮史料縁起由緒続一34">"Atsuta Shrine Historical Records: Continued Compilation of Origins (Part I)": page 34</ref>|group="Note"}}. Another theory holds that the temporary shrine—where the {{ill|Kusanagi no Tsurugi|en|Kusanagi no Tsurugi|qid=Q14944|lt=Grass-cutting Sword}} (also known as the Kusanagi Sword), which was returned to the court in {{ill|686|en|686|qid=Q30619|lt=686}} (the first year of {{ill|Shuchō|en|Shuchō|qid=Q777413|lt=Shuchō}}), was first enshrined—gave the shrine its name<ref name="神宮史料縁起由緒続一184">"Atsuta Shrine Historical Records: Continued Compilation of Origins (Part I)": page 184</ref>. Furthermore, according to the "Owari Chronicle", since the main shrine enshrines five deities—{{ill|Amaterasu|en|Amaterasu|qid=Q455602|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami}}, {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素盞嗚尊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo-no-Mikoto|qid=Q272993}}, {{ill|Yamato Takeru|ja|日本武尊|lt=Prince Yamato Takeru|3=ヤマトタケル|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Takeru no Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Takeru|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ヤマトタケル|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q461258}}, {{ill|Miyasu-hime no Mikoto|ja|宮簀媛命|lt=Miyasu-hime}} and {{ill|Takeinadane|ja|建稲種命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takeinadane no Mikoto|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11486691}}—there is a theory that the name specifically refers to Amaterasu Omikami herself, the foremost of these deities {{#tag:ref|"From 'Owari Chronicle Atsuta': <ref name="尾張志熱田8">page 8</ref> and 'Atsuta Shrine Record': <ref name="神宮史料縁起由緒363"/>"|group="Note"}}. It has also been written as "Ichinokami-mae" (一神前) {{#tag:ref|"From 'Atsuta Shrine Official Enshrinement Record'"<ref name="神宮史料縁起由緒139"/>|group="Note"}}, and as "Ichimusaki" (一御崎) {{#tag:ref|"From 'Atsuta Main and Subsidiary Shrine Divine Body Sacred Decree Collection'"<ref name="神宮史料縁起由緒171">page 171</ref>|group="Note"}}.
